name: Arteme Sans
classification_notes: Modern grotesque with geometric and rational foundations, differentiated from strict neo-grotesques by subtly angled terminals and cuts. Part of the wider Arteme family alongside Arteme Display, which adds higher contrast and tighter spacing for mixed-use editorial settings.
summary: A modern grotesque that channels geometric rigour across five weights and a variable font, distinguished by slightly angled cuts that keep it from feeling cold.
description: Arteme Sans sits between strict neo-grotesque rationalism and something a degree warmer, achieving that through angled terminals rather than obvious humanist cues. Five weights each carry a full italic, and the variable Arteme Sans Flex version adds continuous weight and slant axes. Language support covers 47 Latin-script languages with 524 glyphs per style and a solid OpenType feature set including stylistic alternates, oldstyle figures and a slashed zero.
foundry_blurb: Rellence describes Arteme as a modern grotesque drawn to create tension: unlike most neo-grotesques, it pairs geometric, neutral and rational characteristics with less strict, slightly angled cuts that give it an approachable yet contemporary character. Arteme Display acts as its higher-contrast companion, with tighter spacing for editorial and mixed-weight use.

name: Okima
classification_notes: Monospaced typeface inspired by dot-matrix printer output. Weights are named by ink coverage value (Ink 34 through Ink 200) rather than conventional naming. Each static weight has a corresponding italic, giving 14 styles in total, plus a variable font with weight and italic axes. The design transitions from discrete light dots at lower values to dense, merged strokes at higher ones.
summary: A dot-matrix-inspired monospaced typeface from Rellence with seven ink-density weights, matching italics and a variable font covering both weight and italic axes.
description: Okima translates dot-matrix printer output into a contemporary typeface, naming each weight by its ink coverage rather than the conventional Light–Bold scale. The family runs from Ink 34 – fine, speckled dots – to Ink 200, where strokes are dense and fully merged. Fourteen static styles and a two-axis variable font give it unusual range for a display mono, making it a credible choice for editorial, identity and interface work that wants the texture of retro output hardware.
foundry_blurb: Rellence describes Okima as simulating a range of ink densities, transitioning from delicate light dots to bold heavy ones that flow seamlessly into each other – capturing the aesthetic of dot-matrix printing for both nostalgic and contemporary applications.

name: Albra Book
classification_notes: High-contrast serif with warm curves and sharp bracketed serifs. Albra Book is the fourth optical size in the Albra family, sitting between Albra Text and the standard Albra in contrast and weight. It is the only optical size in the family without italic companions, designed for upright-only body copy at book-setting sizes. Part of a mature multi-optical-size system spanning Display, standard, Book, Text, Sans and Grotesk.
summary: A high-contrast upright-only serif cut as the book optical size in the Albra family, sitting between Albra Text and standard Albra in contrast and weight.
description: Albra Book is the fourth optical size in Jan Weidemüller's Albra family, designed for body copy at book-setting sizes. Sturdier than Albra Text and carrying more visible contrast than a typical workhorse text face, it is the only Albra optical size without italic companions. Six weights run from Light to Black, with a variable font available for continuous weight adjustment.
foundry_blurb: Rellence is a Berlin-based type foundry offering custom and retail typefaces. Their flagship Albra collection spans multiple optical sizes – Display, standard, Book and Text cuts – alongside Albra Sans and Albra Grotesk, forming a comprehensive serif system aimed at editorial, branding and luxury packaging work.

name: Albra Grotesk
classification_notes: Low-contrast grotesque; neutral upright structure with open apertures; single-storey 'a' and variant 'R' alternates available; part of the Albra superfamily alongside a serif, display, text, sans and book variant; Greek and extended Latin character support
summary: A low-contrast grotesque from Jan Weidemüller's Albra superfamily, spanning six weights with full italics and variable font support, built for editorial and luxury branding contexts.
description: Albra Grotesk is the sans companion to Rellence's Albra serif, sharing its restrained, considered aesthetic while removing stroke contrast for cleaner digital utility. Six weights from Light to Black each carry matching italics, and variable font files cover both uprights and italics. OpenType alternates – including a single-storey 'a' and a variant 'R' – give designers enough room to adjust personality without abandoning the family's neutral, refined character.
foundry_blurb: Rellence describes Albra Grotesk as a typeface where raw language meets refined form – a low-contrast sans built on the same tension between order and visual instinct that runs through the wider Albra collection. Aimed at digital luxury and editorial design, it prioritises restraint over personality.

name: Arteme Display
classification_notes: Neo-grotesque display typeface and the high-contrast counterpart to Arteme Sans. Shares the family's geometric-rationalist structure and slightly angled cuts, but with elevated contrast and refined spacing optimised for headline scale. Includes a variable font version (Arteme Display Flex) with Weight and Slant axes.
summary: The high-contrast counterpart to Arteme Sans, this five-weight neo-grotesque display carries tight spacing and refined kerning built for headline work.
description: Part of Rellence's Arteme family, the Display variant heightens contrast and tightens spacing relative to its Sans sibling while sharing the same geometric-rationalist structure and slightly angled cuts. Five weights run from Regular to Black, each with a matching italic, giving 10 static styles in total alongside a variable Flex version with Weight and Slant axes. With 524 glyphs and coverage across 43 languages, it suits branding and editorial work at display scale.
foundry_blurb: Arteme Display is the elegant counterpart to Arteme Sans, featuring higher contrast and tighter spacing and kerning. The Arteme collection is a modern-day grotesque drawn to create tension, combining geometric, neutral and rational characteristics with less strict, slightly angled cuts to deliver an approachable yet modern character and a visually distinctive modernist aesthetic.

name: Albra
classification_notes: Contemporary high-contrast serif with bracketed serifs and a full optical-size range spanning Text, standard and Display cuts. Draws on modern/Didone traditions but softens the historical model with warmer curves and less extreme stroke contrast. Extended system includes grotesque (Albra Grotesk) and sans (Albra Sans) companions, making it one of the more complete retail serif families from an independent foundry. Variable font versions available across the range.
summary: A high-contrast editorial serif with a full optical-size system and grotesque companion, built for fashion, branding and editorial work.
description: Albra is a contemporary serif built around three optical sizes – Text, standard and Display – each calibrated for its intended size range, with Albra Book adding a fourth editorial cut without italics. Jan Weidemüller extended the system with Albra Sans and Albra Grotesk, giving designers a coherent mixed-voice toolkit from a single design source. Sharp bracketed serifs, high contrast and warm curves make the family well suited to fashion editorial, packaging and brand identity work.
foundry_blurb: Rellence – formerly Ultra Kuhl and BumBumType – is a Berlin-based type foundry founded by Jan Weidemüller in 2018. The studio develops retail and custom typefaces focused on contemporary editorial and branding use, and adopted the Rellence name in 2026.

name: Albra Sans
classification_notes: Calligraphy-influenced high-contrast sans-serif with pen-derived stroke variation. Sits between humanist and geometric classifications, retaining the quirkiness of the broader Albra collection while remaining clean enough for extended text and display work. Moderate contrast distinguishes it from both neutral grotesques and dramatic display cuts.
summary: A calligraphy-influenced high-contrast sans-serif from the Albra collection, available in seven weights with matching italics and variable font support.
description: Albra Sans is the sans-serif member of Jan Weidemüller's Albra collection, translating the family's calligraphic stroke contrast into a clean, versatile form. Seven weights from Thin to Black each have matching italics, with both upright and italic variable fonts included. Over 500 glyphs and an extended OpenType feature set – alternates, ligatures, old-style figures – make it well suited to editorial, fashion and branding work.
foundry_blurb: A calligraphy-inspired sans-serif that preserves the Albra collection's characteristic quirkiness. With over 500 glyphs, a broad weight range and an extended stylistic set, it functions as a flexible workhorse across branding and editorial applications.

name: Albra Display
classification_notes: High-contrast bracketed serif with warm rounded curves and sharp serifs. Display-optimised cut of the Albra optical-size family (Text, Regular, Display, Book), tuned for large-scale headline settings. Features alternate 'a' and 'R' glyphs, old-style figures and ligatures. Variable font versions available for both upright and italic axes.
summary: A high-contrast bracketed serif cut for headline use, with warm rounded curves and sharp serifs across six weights from Light to Black.
description: Albra Display is the large-scale cut of Jan Weidemüller's Albra optical-size family, released by Rellence in 2019. Its letterforms push contrast to the display extreme, pairing narrow bracketed serifs with open, rounded bowls that read well in fashion editorial, packaging and branding headlines. All six weights ship with matching italics, and variable font versions cover both upright and italic axes.
foundry_blurb: Rellence – formerly Ultra Kuhl – is a Berlin-based type foundry offering retail and custom typefaces. Albra is the studio's flagship family: a seriffed collection spanning Text, Regular, Display and Book optical sizes, with a Grotesk and a Sans extending the system further.

name: Telka
classification_notes: A wide-bodied geometric sans-serif with consistent stroke thickness and no strong humanist modulation. Width variation is the defining design axis, expressed through three subfamilies (Standard, Extended, Wide) rather than optical sizes. Upright and italic styles share the same geometric rhythm; the Super weight pushes toward display territory.
summary: A geometric sans-serif in three width subfamilies – standard, extended and wide – each spanning six weights with italics, plus a variable font with weight, width and italic axes.
description: Telka is a geometric sans-serif by Berlin-based Jan Weidemüller, built around width as its primary design dimension. Three subfamilies – Telka, Telka Extended and Telka Wide – each cover Light through Super across upright and italic styles, giving 36 static fonts in total alongside a variable font with weight, width and italic axes. With 639 glyphs per style and a solid set of OpenType features including stylistic sets, oldstyle numerals and case-sensitive forms, it sits comfortably across branding, editorial and digital work.
foundry_blurb: Rellence is a Berlin-based independent type foundry run by Jan Weidemüller, previously operating under the name Ultra Kuhl. It produces retail and custom typefaces for brand and editorial use, with a focus on geometric forms and graphic clarity.

name: Albra Text
classification_notes: Low-contrast humanist text serif, the text-size optical member of the Albra family. Bracketed serifs and warm curves echo the high-contrast Albra, but stroke contrast is deliberately reduced to hold legibility at body sizes. Available as both static and variable fonts.
summary: A low-contrast text serif from Jan Weidemüller, optimised for extended reading at smaller sizes as the body-text optical member of the Albra family.
description: Albra Text is the text-size counterpart to the high-contrast Albra series, with reduced stroke contrast to maintain legibility at body sizes on screen and in print. Six weights run from Light to Black, each with a matching italic, and variable font versions cover both axes. Warm curves and bracketed serifs keep it visually consistent with the broader Albra collection.
foundry_blurb: Rellence presents Albra Text as the lower-contrast body-text companion to the wider Albra collection, engineered to perform at sizes where the original Albra's high contrast would compromise legibility, with a stated aim of scaling across digital platforms and print.

name: Porteron
classification_notes: Squared contours with smooth rational curves; disciplined geometric construction with restrained contrast and steady rhythm. Variable font with weight and italic axes. Technical-neutral character, closer to geometric than humanist despite its warmth.
summary: A disciplined geometric sans-serif with squared contours and rational curves, designed for editorial and branding work across five weights with full italic support and a variable font axis.
description: Porteron is built on controlled geometry, its squared terminals and compact-but-open proportions giving it a technical neutrality well suited to layout-heavy work. Five weights span from Regular to Black, each with a matching italic, and a variable font covers both weight and slant axes in a single file. It has been used in real identity projects including Studio Mass's Melbourne Recital Centre branding and Merantix Capital's visual identity by CRU.
foundry_blurb: Rellence describes Porteron as a contemporary sans-serif built on disciplined geometry and controlled proportions, with compact yet open forms combining squared contours and smooth rational curves. The construction feels engineered, characterised by steady rhythm and restrained contrast, intended for boutique labels, archive zines, editorial layouts and branding.

name: Swizzy Mono
classification_notes: Geometric monospace sans with mid-century German Rationalist influence. Fixed-width companion to the Swizzy proportional sans family, maintaining consistent typographic texture across mixed-spacing contexts. Two-axis variable font (weight and italic) available as Swizzy Mono Flex.
summary: The fixed-width companion to Swizzy, carrying the family's geometric mid-century German sensibility into mono form across four weights with matching italics and a two-axis variable version.
description: Swizzy Mono brings Swizzy's geometric clarity into fixed-width form, covering four weights from Regular to Black, each with a matching italic. A two-axis variable font, Swizzy Mono Flex, handles weight and italic in a single file. With 526 glyphs and support for 40-plus languages, it suits technical typesetting, editorial design and branding work where mono spacing is required.
foundry_blurb: Rellence is a Berlin-based type foundry, formerly known as Ultra Kuhl, designing retail and custom typefaces for contemporary brands. Their work emphasises geometric precision and clean letterforms, with the Swizzy family rooted in mid-century German design principles.

name: Telka Extended
classification_notes: A wide-width variant within the Telka family, a contemporary grotesque system with three width cuts (standard, Extended, Wide). Six weights from Light to Super with full italic complement. Variable font available covering weight, width and italic axes. Clean contemporary construction suited to branding and editorial work.
summary: The wider of Telka's three width cuts, offering six weights with italics, variable font support and 40+ language coverage in a clean contemporary grotesque.
description: Designed by Jan Weidemüller and released in 2022, Telka Extended sits alongside standard Telka and Telka Wide in a shared six-weight, italic-inclusive system. A variable font covers weight, width and italic axes in a single file; OpenType features include stylistic sets, oldstyle numerals, ligatures, case-sensitive forms and a slashed zero. The family has seen use across branding, fashion editorial, institutional identity and digital product work.
foundry_blurb: Rellence positions Telka as a typeface built for complex contemporary applications, with standard, extended and wide width variants each spanning six weights and italics. A variable font and 40+ language support are included across the family, with licensing structured by company size and usage type.

name: Swizzy
classification_notes: Geometric sans drawing explicitly on mid-20th century German modernism. Precise, even construction with tight spacing and neutral letterforms. Has a dedicated Mono sub-family and variable font axes for weight and italic. No condensed variant.
summary: A geometric sans rooted in mid-20th century German modernism, offered in seven weights with matching italics, a Mono companion and variable font support across both families.
description: Swizzy takes its cues from the precision and restraint of post-war German type design, translating that tradition into a contemporary geometric sans with clean construction and consistent spacing. Seven weights from Light to Ultra each pair with an italic, and a dedicated Swizzy Mono sub-family covers coding and tabular contexts. Variable font axes for weight and italic keep it practical for performance-sensitive web and app environments.
foundry_blurb: Rellence describes Swizzy as a tribute to legendary typefaces shaped by German design influence, built on the principles of clarity, simplicity and precision inherited from mid-20th century modernism. Geometric letterforms and clean lines aim to balance that historical rigour with contemporary utility, with licensing options spanning brand, web, app and logo use.

name: Aderon
classification_notes: Tightly spaced condensed display sans-serif. Seven static weights (Regular through Dark) each with a true italic, plus Aderon Flex – a variable font with weight and italic axes. No separate condensed subfamily; the compact proportions are intrinsic to the design. Warm curves and moderate contrast. 561 glyphs.
summary: A tightly spaced condensed display sans in seven weights with true italics, designed for confident headlines where column width is tight and personality counts.
description: Aderon is a condensed display sans-serif built for headlines and compact layouts. Its warm curves and consistent proportions keep text clear even at narrow widths, balancing punch with legibility. Seven weights run from Regular to Dark, each with a true italic, and the family is also available as Aderon Flex – a variable font covering weight and italic axes in a single file.
foundry_blurb: Rellence positions Aderon as a tightly spaced display typeface made for confident headlines and compact layouts, with warm curves and consistent proportions that sustain readability in constrained spaces.

name: Telka Wide
classification_notes: Wide-proportioned geometric grotesque; the expanded-width variant of the Telka family, which comes in three widths (Standard, Extended, Wide). Strong geometry with idiosyncratic details. Variable font available spanning weight, width and italic axes. Six weights from Light to Super, each with an italic.
summary: A wide-proportioned geometric grotesque with six weights and full italics, built for brand systems and large-format display work.
description: Telka Wide is the expanded-width variant of Jan Weidemüller's Telka family, stretching a geometric grotesque skeleton into characterful proportions with distinctive detail. Six weights from Light to Super each carry an italic, and a variable font covers weight, width and italic axes in a single file. Clear without being neutral, it suits editorial headlines, brand identities and environmental signage across 43+ Latin languages.
foundry_blurb: Rellence positions Telka as one idea realised across six weights and three width variants – Standard, Extended and Wide – built to scale from pitch decks to public installations. The Wide subfamily trades neutrality for personality, with quirky character details that give it presence at any size.

name: Matiere
classification_notes: High-contrast display serif that blends calligraphic stroke qualities with contemporary geometric precision. Rellence describes the balance as "brutal precision and elegant airiness," drawing on mid-century design references. No italics; all styles are upright. Two-axis variable font spans weight and width axes.
summary: A high-contrast display serif fusing calligraphic stroke with contemporary precision, offered in six weights across standard and condensed widths with a two-axis variable font.
description: Matiere draws on calligraphic motion and mid-century references to produce a high-contrast display serif with what Rellence calls "brutal precision and elegant airiness." It runs six weights in both standard and condensed widths, backed by a two-axis variable font covering weight and width. The family suits branding, editorial, packaging and luxury contexts where typographic presence needs to hold at large sizes.
foundry_blurb: Rellence describes Matiere as a spacious exploration of high-contrast serif display possibilities, fusing calligraphic motion with contemporary precision across digital and print media.

name: Arnet
classification_notes: Geometric modernist sans-serif drawing on mid-century German rationalism and Swiss typographic precision. Uniform character widths, rounded warm curves cut with sharp terminals, large x-height, and moderate stroke contrast. Originally released in 2019 under the name Gram before being renamed Arnet.
subfamilies: Arnet Flex (variable font, weight and italic axes)
summary: A geometric sans-serif fusing mid-century German rationalism with Swiss precision across ten weights and a variable font.
description: Arnet pairs the sturdy logic of German modernist sans-serifs with Swiss typographic discipline, producing a face that balances warm curves against sharp cuts. A large x-height and moderate stroke contrast sustain legibility across editorial, branding and wayfinding contexts. Ten weights and twenty styles in total, plus a variable font with weight and italic axes, make it a practical choice for systems work.
foundry_blurb: Berlin-based type foundry offering retail and custom typefaces. Originally founded as Ultra Kühl, rebranded as Rellence in 2026. Clients include Apple Music, BBC and Bloomberg.

name: Sace
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif with prominent ink traps across five weights; paired with a Tiltalic collection at a steep 45-degree angle. Variable font versions (Sace Flex and Sace Tiltalic Flex) available with a single weight axis. Over 530 glyphs per style with full OpenType feature set.
summary: A geometric sans with prominent ink traps in five weights, paired with a steep 45-degree Tiltalic collection and variable font support.
description: Sace is a geometric sans-serif defined by prominent ink traps that sharpen legibility at smaller sizes without sacrificing texture at display scale. Five weights run from Regular to Ultra, each matched by a Tiltalic counterpart angled at 45 degrees — not a conventional italic, but a deliberately rhythmic slant that adds movement to layouts. Variable font versions cover both families on a single weight axis, and the character set reaches 43 languages across 530-plus glyphs with a full OpenType feature set including ligatures, fractions and case-sensitive forms.
foundry_blurb: Rellence describes Sace as combining modern aesthetics with functional ink trap enhancements for exceptional legibility in digital and print environments. The Tiltalic variant creates unexpected rhythm through its steep 45-degree angle, intended to bring movement and distinction to design campaigns.

name: Siaga
classification_notes: Proportional geometric sans drawing openly on monospaced modernist traditions. Even stroke contrast, restrained terminals and consistent apertures produce a mechanical evenness without the rigidity of a true fixed-width face. Sits in the neighbourhood of DIN and Eurostile in spirit, but lighter and more refined. Not monospaced – the foundry's own description frames it as preserving proportional widths while referencing the aesthetic.
summary: A proportional geometric sans that channels monospaced modernist aesthetics across seven weights, 14 styles and a variable font covering both weight and italic axes.
description: Siaga began in 2015 as a bespoke typeface for Studio Weidemüller's visual identity before being comprehensively redrawn over four years into a full retail collection. Its even spacing and clean terminals carry a clear debt to monospaced modernist type, giving the family a metrically consistent colour from Thin to Ultra while remaining proportional throughout. OpenType features include four stylistic alternates, oldstyle and tabular numerals, a slashed zero and standard ligatures, making it capable across display and extended text settings.
foundry_blurb: Rellence is an independent type foundry based in Berlin, founded by Jan Weidemüller in 2018 under the name Ultra Kühl, merged with BumBumType in 2021 and rebranded as Rellence in January 2026. The foundry produces retail and custom typefaces for brand and editorial applications.

name: Matiere Condensed
classification_notes: High-contrast display serif drawing on calligraphic stroke tension; upright only with no italic cuts; the condensed subfamily of the broader Matiere family, which spans standard and condensed widths plus a variable font with weight and width axes.
summary: A high-contrast condensed display serif in six weights, pairing calligraphic stroke tension with precise contemporary construction.
description: Matiere Condensed is the narrow companion to Rellence's standard Matiere family, sharing six weights from Light to Super. The design merges sharp stroke contrast with calligraphic rhythm, lending it authority in luxury branding, packaging and editorial headline work. A variable font covering weight and width axes is also available for those who want finer control across the full family.
foundry_blurb: Rellence describes Matiere as the product of a broad exploration of high-contrast serif display typefaces, built around the idea of fusing the qualities of calligraphic motion with contemporary precision.

name: Sace Tiltalic
classification_notes: The slanted companion to the Sace grotesque family, angled at an unconventional 45° rather than a conventional italic incline. Features prominent ink traps throughout. Ships with a one-axis variable Flex version. Catalogued separately from the upright Sace family.
summary: A grotesque with pronounced ink traps whose italic form tilts at an unconventional 45° angle, giving it a distinctive rhythmic presence suited to fashion, editorial and high-contrast brand work.
description: Sace Tiltalic is the slanted companion to the Sace grotesque, angled at 45° rather than a conventional italic incline — a decision that produces an unusual, kinetic feel on the page. Prominent ink traps sharpen each letterform for clarity in both print and digital contexts. It ships in five weights with a one-axis variable Flex version, covering 43+ languages across the Latin Extended range with 551 glyphs and OpenType features including stylistic sets, contextual alternates and tabular figures.
foundry_blurb: Rellence (formerly Ultra Kühl) is a type foundry that designs retail and custom typefaces for brands, distributed exclusively through its own website for direct licensing and support. Clients include Apple Music, BBC, Bloomberg and Moncler.

name: Para Grand
classification_notes: Para Grand is the display optical size of the Para family, which spans three optical variants: Superior (small text), Central (medium), and Grand (display). It sits in geometric grotesque territory with some humanist warmth and high-contrast influence drawn loosely from Didone and Transitional traditions. Six weights from Light to Super, all with matching italics, plus variable font versions (Para Grand Flex and Para Grand Italic Flex on a single weight axis). 673 glyphs per style with a full OpenType feature set including small caps, oldstyle and tabular figures, ligatures and fractions.
summary: A contemporary geometric grotesque designed for display use, the largest of three optical sizes in Rellence's Para family, available in six weights with italics and variable font support.
description: Para Grand is the display-scale variant of the Para family, which Rellence positions across three optical sizes to cover text, mid-scale and headline settings. It carries six weights from Light to Super, each with a matching italic, and ships with variable font versions on a weight axis. The design mixes geometric structure with high-contrast details drawn from Didone and Transitional references, landing somewhere between cold precision and editorial warmth.
foundry_blurb: Rellence (formerly Ultra Kuhl) is a German type foundry founded by Jan Weidemüller, producing retail and custom typefaces. Their work spans editorial serif families like Albra through to contemporary grotesques, with a stated interest in combining beauty and brutality across optical-size systems built for professional publishing contexts.

name: Alyc
classification_notes: Modern rounded sans-serif with a deliberate two-tier approach to roundness: terminals are fully circular while stems are only semi-rounded. Variable font with weight and italic axes. 565-glyph character set with comprehensive OpenType features including stylistic alternates, oldstyle figures, tabular numerals and slashed zero.
summary: A rounded grotesk with fully circular terminals and semi-rounded stems, striking a warm, approachable balance across six weights and a two-axis variable font.
description: Alyc applies roundness with restraint: terminals are completely circular while stems stay semi-rounded, giving the face friendliness without tipping into novelty. Six weights run from Light to Black, each paired with a true italic, and a two-axis variable font covers the full weight and slant range in a single file. The 565-glyph set includes stylistic alternates, old-style and tabular figures, case-sensitive forms and a slashed zero – enough for professional editorial and branding work.
foundry_blurb: Rellence is a type foundry founded by Jan Weidemüller, previously operating as Ultra Kühl from 2018. The studio absorbed BumBumType in 2021 and rebranded as Rellence in January 2026, producing retail and custom typefaces oriented towards contemporary graphic and digital design.

name: Blak
classification_notes: Neoclassical blackletter stripped of decorative elements and rebuilt on strict geometric principles. Five widths (Tight to Zoom) across three style variants (upright, slanted, backslanted), plus a two-axis variable font. The geometry is absolute – no optical corrections, no calligraphic softening – giving it an industrial, modular feel closer to a grid system than traditional fraktur.
summary: A geometric display blackletter that strips fraktur back to a strict grid, available in five widths across upright, slanted and backslanted cuts plus a two-axis variable font.
description: Blak takes the structure of blackletter and removes everything calligraphic, applying pure geometry and strict design rules in its place. The result is a bold, modular display face that reads as a contemporary design system rather than a historical revival. Fifteen static fonts span five widths from Tight to Zoom across three style variants, with a variable font (Blak Flex) adding a Weight axis alongside Italic.
foundry_blurb: Rellence describes Blak as a neoclassical blackletter-inspired display typeface built by eliminating unnecessary decoration and applying strict design rules – pure geometric shapes on a strict grid, optimised for large display use across editorial, retail, environmental, web, film and physical media contexts.

name: Mondara
classification_notes: High-contrast serif with bracketed serifs and generous rounded forms. Strong vertical stress and horizontal serifs give it a contemporary crispness while the rounded proportions soften any rigidity. Sits between transitional and modern in historical terms, but designed and positioned squarely for display use at large sizes. No text cuts exist.
summary: High-contrast display serif with bracketed serifs and rounded forms, built for branding, packaging and large-scale display use.
description: Mondara pairs generous rounded letterforms with sharp stroke contrast and finely bracketed serifs, giving it the precision of a modern face alongside classical warmth. Four weights run from Regular to Black, with a single-axis variable font covering the full range and 477 glyphs per style. No italic or condensed cuts exist, making it a dedicated display choice with good multilingual coverage across 43+ European languages.
foundry_blurb: Rellence is a Berlin-based type foundry creating retail and custom typefaces for brand-defining work. Founded by Jan Weidemüller as Ultra Kuhl in 2018 and rebranded as Rellence in 2025, the foundry offers flexible licensing aimed at agencies and independent brands.

name: Para Superior
classification_notes: Contemporary sans drawing from Didone and Transitional type traditions. The Superior cut is the display-grade optical size of the Para family, alongside Grand and Central. Rellence specifies a contrast index of 3.4 and a 1.2 spacing ratio. Described by the foundry as "curved, modern, feminine — like Gill Sans with makeup."
summary: Para Superior is Rellence's display-grade optical cut of the Para family, a contemporary sans drawing from Didone and Transitional sources, with seven weights, matching italics and a variable weight axis.
description: Para Superior sits at the top of the three-cut Para system alongside Central and Grand, each offering seven weights with matching italics. It draws from Didone and Transitional traditions to arrive at a contemporary, curve-forward sans suited to editorial headlines, logotypes and packaging. A variable weight-axis version (Para Superior Flex) and 673 glyphs per style with 43+ language support complete the offering.
foundry_blurb: Rellence — formerly Ultra Kühl, rebranded in January 2026 — was founded by Jan Weidemüller and describes Para as "beautiful and brutal": a reinterpretation of Didone and Transitional typefaces distilled into a minimalistic, contemporary form. Positioned as a growing, versatile family for editorial, corporate, web, packaging and logotype work.

name: Para Central
classification_notes: Text-optimised optical member of the three-part Para family (Central / Grand / Superior). Developed from Didone and Transitional sources, retaining high stroke contrast while stripping the forms back into a spare, contemporary sans-serif. Para Central is the body-text cut; Para Superior handles display at the other end of the hierarchy.
summary: Para Central is the body-text cut of Rellence's Para optical-size system, a high-contrast sans drawn from Didone and Transitional principles, available in six weights with paired italics and variable font.
description: Para Central is the body-text member of Rellence's Para family, which spans three optical sizes – Central, Grand and Superior – each offered in six weights with italic counterparts. The design traces its origins to Didone and Transitional serif traditions, evolving those high-contrast principles into a spare, contemporary form suited to editorial, corporate, packaging and logotype work. Each weight ships with a single-axis variable font, and OpenType support covers small caps, tabular and oldstyle numerals, discretionary ligatures and a slashed zero.
foundry_blurb: Rellence describe Para as a typeface conceived to be both beautiful and brutal, developed over several years from Didone and Transitional roots into a minimal, contemporary form. The family is built to scale from pitch decks to public installations, with three optical sizes engineered for design systems across editorial, corporate, web, packaging and logotype applications.
